elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to both Parties.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 limits “each Party's total aggregate liability” and expressly states that the cap is mutual.

elements.element: The fee-based limb of the cap equals fees paid or payable during the 12 months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: The clause uses “all amounts paid or payable” rather than fees and measures the period preceding “the event giving rise to the claim,” not the claim itself.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of the applicable 12-month fee amount and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 expressly applies the greater of its 12-month amount and USD 1,000,000, although its 12-month amount does not precisely match the required fee limb.

elements.element: Indirect damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: No operative language excludes indirect damages.

elements.element: Consequential damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: No operative language excludes consequential damages.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The clause excludes “Excluded Claims” from the cap, but no operative definition establishing that confidentiality breaches are Excluded Claims is provided. The margin comment is non-operative.

elements.element: Liability for breach of data protection obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The supplied operative language does not establish that data protection breaches are Excluded Claims.

result.reason: The redline establishes a mutual greater-of cap with a USD 1,000,000 floor, but it does not establish either complete position. Its fee limb uses the broader phrase “all amounts” and a different measurement trigger, while the fallback requires a straight 12-month-fee cap. More importantly, the operative text supplied does not define Excluded Claims, so none of the required carve-outs can be verified; the margin comment cannot cure that omission. The clause also omits the preferred mutual indirect/consequential-damages exclusion and payment-obligation treatment. The edit remains focused on liability allocation and does not appear to disturb unrelated commercial terms, but it is not minimal to a complete level because no complete level is achieved and the “all amounts” formulation is broader than the required fee basis.
